summary: The Secret of the Sunless is a project that explores whether life could exist in environments without direct sunlight. It focuses on rogue planets and icy ocean worlds, investigating the conditions that could support life in complete darkness. Even without sunlight, a planet's internal heat may keep underground oceans in a liquid state, while certain microorganisms could use chemical energy to survive. The project is important because it shows that life may not be limited to environments similar to Earth's surface and that sunlight is not essential for every possible form of life. In this type of world, the surface could be extremely cold and dark, while liquid oceans might exist beneath thick layers of ice. Chemical reactions could provide energy for potential microbial life in these hidden oceans. Through scientific explanations, calculations, and interactive scenarios, the project helps students understand how such environments might work. However, it presents extraterrestrial life as a scientific possibility, not as a confirmed discovery.

Detailed Project Description – The Secret of the Sunless

Our project, The Secret of the Sunless, explores whether life could exist in environments without direct sunlight. It combines an educational video with an interactive learning prototype called Sunless Worlds Explorer. The project focuses on two different scenarios: free-floating rogue planets and icy ocean worlds.

While working on this project, our team investigated not only whether life could exist without sunlight but also what would happen if such life actually existed. We explored what kind of environment it would live in, which energy sources it could use, and how its living conditions might be different from those on Earth. We especially focused on internal planetary heat, liquid water beneath ice layers, and chemical energy sources.

Our proposed prototype aims to explain how internal heat, insulation, liquid water, and chemical energy could create suitable conditions for life in dark environments. It is designed to include adjustable parameters, energy-pathway diagrams, and comparisons between two planetary scenarios. Users will be able to explore how changing different conditions affects the results. We also use the mathematical relationship ΔT ≈ qd/k to demonstrate heat conduction and temperature changes.

The main benefit of our project is making a complex scientific subject, astrobiology, easier and more interesting for students to understand. We aim to encourage people to think beyond Earth's conditions and explore different possibilities for life in the universe.

During our research and development process, we used NASA resources to access scientific information, Canva to create visual designs and prepare our presentation and educational video, and ChatGPT to develop ideas, organize information, and support the content creation process.

The creativity of our project comes from combining scientific research, visual storytelling, physics calculations, and interactive learning. Our team considered scientific accuracy, energy sources, liquid water stability, chemical energy, data reliability, and scientific uncertainties. Rather than claiming that extraterrestrial life has been discovered, we present it as a scientific possibility worth investigating.
